items.q: Jo Jones. I used to carry his drums to record dates and set them up, and carry his drums and get coffee for him and all that stuff. Like an apprentice

ctx.x: Jo Jones. I used to carry his drums to record dates and set them up, and carry his drums and get coffee for him and all that stuff. Like an apprentice, which the young guys won’t do that now. I learned so much that it’s just like you took him out of college. That was like, you know, just watching him play in all these different venues. I’d carry his drums, set them up, take them down, you know what I mean, take them home for him if he wanted to go somewhere else. And he told me one day, he used to say “Well meet…
Boy, I bet you’re glad you went though.

items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: We met Papa Jo Jones, who took us into his apartment and kept us for about — we lived with him for about two years.

ctx.x: Or the opposite. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

Or the opposite, right, yes, absolutely. The time thing is very elusive. It’s not like — as Papa Jo Jones used to say, jazz is something special just like classical music is special in its idiom, but jazz is just as special because it’s different. And the time thing is completely different. And when you’re playing jazz, oh I don’t know if it was an old guy or a young guy that always told me — I told these kids up at this college I went to — a lot of people have never heard about the pendulum. items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: You know two little kids that stayed with me, Oliver Jackson and Eddie Locke. I used to tell them, 'You're going to play with Earl Hines...'

ctx.x: We had that. When you was in this category you played into this club. You did not go over here and play into this club until you qualified, then you begin to move up and you sit in over here. Then as I said, the older guys when they got ready to semi-retire, they went and got a young man and set him down in the home and gave him the book and they went to the bandleader and said, "He's taking my place." But they don't have that now because

we've had a hectic situation for 22 years. But we could never know, with all this wealth of talent out here - and we're not in a position, we don't travel around even though we got the airplane and everything - we're not in a position because we're not set in our views. We've gone into certain things. Like I'm with a drum shop for 2 years and my heart bleeds that I can't go out and give this.
